_comment: The ready-made pictures behind the image overlay's Assets button (see
js/assets.js). Adding one is a PNG dropped into this folder and an
entry below; nothing else has to change.
`file` is the PNG's name in this folder. `name` is what the picker
shows under it. `color` is the one colour the asset is painted in,
and it does two jobs: it is the colour the picker opens on, and it is
the colour that gets REPLACED when the user chooses another.
That second job is why it has to be right. The recolouring treats
every pixel as some amount of `color` laid over a neutral grey, so a
drop shadow, a white highlight, or the soft edge where the paint
meets either keeps its shading and only the paint changes. An asset
drawn in two different colours would have the second one shifted
along with the first, so an asset is one colour plus greys, black
and white — and `color` names that one colour exactly.
And no shadow of its own. The colour step has a Drop shadow switch
and draws the shadow itself (see assets.js), so a shadow baked into
the PNG is one the user could not switch off, and doubled when they
switch the other on. ring.png and both arrows arrived with one and
had it taken out; the arrows' black outline is a grey like any other
to the recolouring, so it stays black whatever colour is picked.
